title: Water inside the car
h1: Why is there water inside my car?
metaDesc: Wet carpet or water inside your car? Answer a few questions to find where it's getting in, how urgent it is, and what to tell your mechanic.
intro: Water inside a car usually comes from a blocked drain, a worn seal or a clogged A/C drain. Where the water shows up, and when, is a strong clue to the cause. Answer a few questions to find the likely source and how quickly you should deal with it.
safety: If the liquid smells sweet or the inside of the windshield fogs with a greasy film, watch the temperature gauge. If it climbs, pull over and turn off the engine.
If the car sat in water deep enough to reach the floor or seats, don't start it until it's been inspected.
If you smell burning or see smoke from under the dash or seats, turn the car off and get out.

q_type.help: Press a white paper towel into the wet carpet and smell it. Coolant is often green, orange or pink and smells sweet.

result.title: The heater core may be leaking coolant into the cabin
result.now: Check the coolant level when the engine is cold, top it up if needed, and get the car checked within a few days. Keep the windows cracked while you drive.
if: If the temperature gauge rises above normal, pull over and turn off the engine. Don't restart it.
If the windshield fogs so badly you can't see, don't drive it until it's fixed.
If the coolant level is dropping fast, don't drive it. Have it towed.
If steam or hot liquid comes from the vents or under the dash, pull over, turn the engine off and get out.
If the fumes make your eyes sting or give you a headache, open the windows and stop driving.
result.why: The heater core is a small radiator behind the dashboard. When it leaks, hot coolant can soak the passenger carpet and its vapor leaves a greasy, sweet-smelling film on the glass. You're losing coolant, and the vapor isn't something you want to breathe.

causes.name: Leaking heater core
causes.clues: A sweet smell inside, a greasy film on the windshield, and wet passenger carpet.
causes.against: If the liquid is plain water with no smell, this is unlikely.

causes.name: Leaking heater hose connection
causes.clues: Coolant loss and wetness near the firewall, where the hoses go into the dash.

causes.name: Blocked A/C drain
causes.clues: The water is clear and odorless, and it happens after running the A/C.
causes.against: A sweet smell points away from this.

you: Check the coolant level when the engine is cold.
Smell the wet carpet and look for a greasy film on the inside of the windshield.
shop: Check for coolant in the HVAC case

result.title: The A/C drain may be blocked
result.now: Look under the car near the passenger footwell while the A/C runs. If no water drips out, the drain tube may be clogged. Book a check to have it cleared and the carpet dried.
if: If the carpet stays wet for more than a few days, have it dried properly to prevent mold and damage to wiring under the floor.
If the water smells sweet, it may be coolant, not A/C water. Check your coolant level.
result.why: The A/C pulls water out of the air and drains it through a small tube under the car. If leaves, dirt or insects block that tube, the water backs up and spills onto the passenger floor instead.

causes.name: Clogged A/C evaporator drain
causes.clues: No drip under the car when the A/C runs, and a wet passenger floor on dry days.

causes.name: Drain tube kinked or disconnected
causes.clues: It started after work behind the dashboard.

causes.name: Heater core leak
causes.clues: The water smells sweet or the windshield fogs with a film.
causes.against: Plain, odorless water points away from this.

you: Run the A/C for 10 minutes on a warm day and check for a drip under the car.
Feel the carpet after an A/C-only drive with no rain.

result.title: Rainwater may be getting in at the base of the windshield
result.now: Open the hood and clear any leaves or debris from the vented panel below the windshield, then book a check if it still leaks.
if: If water reaches the fuse box or wiring under the dash, or electrical things start acting up, get it checked within a few days.
If the carpet stays wet, have it dried to prevent mold.
If you smell burning or see smoke from under the dash or seats, turn the car off and get out. If the airbag light or other warning lights come on, have it checked before relying on the car.
result.why: The area below the windshield, called the cowl, collects rainwater and drains it away. When its drains clog with leaves, water can overflow into the fresh-air intake or past seals and end up on the passenger floor.

causes.name: Clogged cowl drains
causes.clues: Leaves or debris in the panel below the windshield, and it's worse after heavy rain.

causes.name: Windshield seal leak
causes.clues: Water appears high up, near the top of the dash or the pillar.

causes.name: Missing cabin air filter cover or seal
causes.clues: Recent cabin filter replacement.

you: Clear leaves and debris from the cowl area.
Have someone run a garden hose over the windshield base while you watch inside.
shop: Water test of the cowl, windshield and door seals

result.title: A door seal, windshield seal or body drain may be letting rain in
result.now: Dry the carpet and book a water test so a shop can find exactly where it's getting in.
if: If the carpet stays wet or smells musty, have it dried properly to prevent mold.
If electrical things start acting up, get it checked within a few days. Wiring and modules often sit under the carpet.
If you smell burning or see smoke from under the dash or seats, turn the car off and get out. If the airbag light or other warning lights come on, have it checked before relying on the car.
result.why: Rubber seals harden and shrink with age, and doors have drain holes at the bottom that can clog. Either one lets rain or car wash water work its way into the footwell.

causes.name: Worn or damaged door seal
causes.clues: Water near the door sill, or light visible around the closed door.

causes.name: Clogged door drain holes
causes.clues: Water sloshing inside the door, or a wet sill after rain.

causes.name: Windshield or cowl leak
causes.clues: Water appears at the top of the footwell, near the dash.

you: Look for torn or flattened rubber seals around the door.
Check that the drain holes at the bottom of the door are clear.

result.title: The sunroof drains may be clogged
result.now: Open the sunroof and slowly pour a cup of water into the channel near a corner. It should drain out under the car within a few seconds. If it pools, that drain is clogged.
if: If the water doesn't drain, have a shop clear the drains. Forcing high-pressure air into them can pop the hoses loose.
If water drips near the dome light or airbag areas, or electrical things act up, get it checked within a few days.
If you smell burning or see smoke from under the dash or seats, turn the car off and get out. If the airbag light or other warning lights come on, have it checked before relying on the car.
result.why: Sunroofs aren't watertight. They catch water in a tray and send it out through small hoses in the roof pillars. When those hoses clog or come loose, water overflows into the headliner and runs down the pillars.

causes.name: Clogged sunroof drain tubes
causes.clues: Water pools in the sunroof channel instead of draining.

causes.name: Disconnected or cracked drain tube
causes.clues: Water drains from the channel but still ends up inside, often down a pillar.

causes.name: Worn sunroof seal
causes.clues: It leaks only in heavy rain, around the glass edge.

you: Pour a little water into each corner of the sunroof channel and watch where it goes.
Look for water stains on the headliner near the pillars.
shop: Sunroof drain cleaning and tube inspection

result.title: A windshield, roof or roof-rack seal may be leaking
result.now: Dry the area, then book a water test to find where it's getting in.
if: If water drips near the dome light, airbag covers or other wiring, get it checked within a few days.
If the headliner stays damp or smells musty, have it dried to prevent mold.
If you smell burning or see smoke from under the dash or seats, turn the car off and get out. If the airbag light or other warning lights come on, have it checked before relying on the car.
result.why: Without a sunroof, water coming through the roof area usually gets past the windshield seal, a roof-rack mount or an antenna base. These leaks often show up at the headliner or run down a pillar.

causes.name: Windshield seal leak
causes.clues: Water at the top corners of the windshield, especially after a windshield replacement.

causes.name: Roof rack or antenna mount seal
causes.clues: A drip spot directly below the rack or antenna.

causes.name: Rear window or hatch seal
causes.clues: Water near the back of the headliner.

you: Look for water stains on the headliner and note where they start.
Check whether the windshield was replaced recently.

result.title: Water in the rear may be coming past a door seal, drain or body plug
result.now: Lift the floor mats to see how wet it is, dry it out, and book a water test.
if: If the car has a sunroof, check the rear sunroof drains too. They often empty near the rear doors.
If the carpet stays wet, have it dried properly to prevent mold and corrosion.
If you smell burning or see smoke from under the dash or seats, turn the car off and get out. If the airbag light or other warning lights come on, have it checked before relying on the car.
result.why: Rear footwells usually get wet from rear door seals, clogged door drains or a missing rubber plug in the floor. On cars with a sunroof, a blocked rear drain can also send water down the back pillars.

causes.name: Rear door seal or clogged door drains
causes.clues: Water near the rear door sills after rain.

causes.name: Missing or loose floor plug
causes.clues: It gets wet after driving through puddles, not just after rain.

causes.name: Rear sunroof drain
causes.clues: Water stains on the rear pillars or headliner.

you: Check the rear door seals and the drain holes at the bottom of the doors.
Look under the carpet for wet padding.

result.title: A trunk seal, taillight gasket or body plug may be leaking
result.now: Lift the trunk floor and check the spare tire well for water, then look for cracked taillights or a torn trunk seal.
if: If water keeps collecting, book a water test so it doesn't cause rust in the floor.
If there's wiring or a battery in the trunk area, get it checked within a few days.
If you smell burning or see smoke from the trunk area, turn the car off and get out.
result.why: Trunks commonly leak through worn lid seals, taillight gaskets or a rear window seal. Water often collects unseen in the spare tire well and can lead to rust and a musty smell.

causes.name: Taillight gasket
causes.clues: Water trails below the taillights inside the trunk.

causes.name: Trunk lid or hatch seal
causes.clues: Water near the trunk opening after rain.

causes.name: Missing or loose body plug
causes.clues: Water in the spare tire well after driving in wet weather.

you: Check the spare tire well.
Look for cracked taillights and torn seals.

result.title: Water may have gotten into the engine, electrical system or airbags
result.now: Don't start the car. Have it towed to a shop and contact your insurance company.
if: If the car is already running and the water was only at the bottom of the doors, turn it off and have it inspected before relying on it.
If the engine stalled while driving through water, don't try to restart it. That can badly damage the engine.
If you smell burning or see smoke, get out and stay away from the car.
result.why: Deep water can get into the engine's air intake, which can wreck the engine if you start it. It can also soak wiring, computers and airbag parts under the seats and carpet, causing problems that show up weeks later.

causes.name: Water entering through door seals and floor openings
causes.clues: Wet carpet and padding after deep water.

causes.name: Water in the engine air intake
causes.clues: The engine stalled in the water or won't turn over normally.

causes.name: Water in electrical connectors and modules
causes.clues: Warning lights, odd electrical behavior, or a musty smell later on.

you: Note how high the water came on the outside of the car.
Take photos for your insurance company.
shop: Air intake and engine oil check for water
Carpet and padding removal to dry the floor

result.title: A water test will show where it's getting in
result.now: Dry the carpet, then on a dry day run the A/C for 10 minutes and check the floor. If it's still dry, have someone run a garden hose over the car while you watch inside.
if: If it only gets wet with the A/C on, the A/C drain may be blocked.
If it smells sweet or the windshield fogs with a greasy film, check your coolant level. It may be the heater core.
If you smell burning or see smoke from under the dash or seats, turn the car off and get out. If the airbag light or other warning lights come on, have it checked before relying on the car.
result.why: Most interior water comes from either the A/C drain or a rain leak. Testing them one at a time, A/C first and then a hose, tells you which one, and a shop can pinpoint it from there.

causes.name: Blocked A/C drain
causes.clues: Wet passenger floor after A/C use, even on dry days.

causes.name: Clogged cowl or body drains
causes.clues: It's worse after heavy rain or a car wash.

causes.name: Worn door or windshield seal
causes.clues: Water near a door sill or the top of the dash.

you: Test with the A/C first, then with a hose.
Feel under the carpet to see where it's wettest.
